name: June Bud
lede: June Bud is a yellow-green named for the color of a leaf bud opening in early summer.

sections.title: The color of a new leaf
sections.body:
Our library traces the name only to a Wikipedia color list, which gives no date or coiner [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 lists eight near-synonyms in the same measured block, including Brill, Glory Green and Jade Lime, a sign this general shade of yellow-green had many competing commercial names [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[yellowish-green]], 4.8 units of CIEDE2000 away and more vivid [1]. [[oil-yellow]] sits at the same distance but duller, and [[inchworm]] a little farther at 5.6, more vivid and lighter [1]. Measured in LCH, June Bud sits at lightness 83 with a strong yellow-green hue, among the brightest, most saturated colors in our library [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This exact swatch is one of the rarest in our archive: only 2 of 23,781 paintings match it, rarer than 82 percent of the named colors, as photographed [2]. Both are from a single 1910 painting by Othon Friesz [2]. Werner's 1821 nomenclature, built from mineral, animal and plant examples rather than museum paintings, lists a close match within 8.3 units at its Siskin Green entry, exemplified by a ripening pear and the Irish pitcher apple [3]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [2].
